sections.title: Interview bank U03: Transformer accounting and speculative inference

keyTerms.definition: Original practice, role-derived material. Not actual lab questions.
A set of breadth, ladder, analytical, debug, scenario, and critique questions per unit.

recall.question: What is the provenance of this interview bank?
recall.answer: Original practice, role-derived. The questions are not actual lab questions.

keyTerms.definition: 12LnTD: dominates past T ~ 6n.
Draft cheaply, verify in parallel; speedup = E[k]/(gamma*c+1).
Accept with min(1, p(x)/q(x)); resample from norm(max(0, p-q)).
Output distributed exactly as the target model p.

recall.question: Write the full training FLOP formula with the attention term. When does the attention term dominate?
recall.answer: C = 6PD + 12LnTD. Attention dominates past T ~ 6n (at T=32768, n=4096 it exceeds dense).

recall.question: Define the speculative decoding speedup formula with all symbols.
Write the token acceptance rule. What distribution does a rejected token get resampled from?
recall.answer: Accept with min(1, p(x)/q(x)). Resample from norm(max(0, p-q)).

keyTerms.definition: Expected accepted tokens per round: sum a^i plus the bonus token.
Draft-to-target step-time ratio.
Real acceptance declines with position; the formula assumes it flat.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 works the speculative decoding economics at c=0.05, a=0.8, gamma=5. What are E[k] and the speedup, and when does it lose?
recall.answer: E[k] = 3.689, speedup 2.95x. At a=0.3, c=0.5: E[k]=1.42, cost 3.5, 0.41x: a 2.4x slowdown.

keyTerms.definition: q*min(1,p/q) = min(q,p).
p - min(q,p) = max(0,p-q), covered by resampling.
Draft and target must share the vocabulary, or the identity fails.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 proves speculative sampling is exact. What is the one-position proof?
recall.answer: Accept mass: q*min(1,p/q) = min(q,p). Residual: p - min(q,p) = max(0,p-q), covered by resample. Sum = p.

keyTerms.definition: 6PD: the non-attention training FLOPs.
The acceptance rate where E[k] = gamma*c+1.
Attention FLOPs over total; 55.3% at T=32768 on the toy.

recall.question: P=7e9, D=1e12, L=32, n=4096. Compute the dense term 6PD and the attention term 12LnTD at T=2048 and T=32768.
a=0.9, gamma=7, c=0.1. Compute E[k] and the speedup. Find the break-even a.

keyTerms.definition: Accept probability must be min(1, p/q), never raw p/q.
Over many rounds the output histogram equals p.

recall.question: D1. The acceptance loop is meant to implement speculative sampling, but the output distribution is wrong. What is the bug, the fix, and the invariant?
recall.answer: Bugs: (1) accept probability p[x]/q[x] not capped at 1, (2) on reject no resample from norm(max(0,p-q)): the residual mass is dropped. Invariant: over many rounds the output histogram equals p.

keyTerms.definition: c=0 but verification costs 1+0.1*gamma steps.
At batch 256 the free-verification assumption breaks.
Grid over gamma; peak should match the formula within 1-2 steps.

recall.question: The draft model is free (c=0) but verification costs 1+0.1*gamma steps. What is the new speedup formula and the best gamma at a=0.8?
Batch is 256 (compute-bound decode). Does speculative decoding still help?
recall.answer: At batch 256 decode is compute-bound: the free-verification assumption breaks. The cost model gains a compute term; speedup shrinks and can flip. It is a latency/batch-1 technique.

keyTerms.definition: Draft and target must share the tokenizer.
Measured a on what workload? Cherry-picked prompts invalidate.

recall.question: A paper claims “3x faster generation with no quality loss” for a new draft architecture. What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) Same tokenizer? (2) Measured a on what workload? (3) Is the baseline the fastest non-speculative serving? (4) Quality metric proving no loss? (5) End-to-end latency with draft overhead?
